pll2d12c5-d1e3519.summary: Raises two questions: why the confused matter is called unformed, whether it lacked all form; and where it came to be and how high it reached.

pll2d12c5-d1e3524.summary: Answers that the first matter is not called unformed because it had no form, since nothing bodily can lack all form, but because, confused and mixed, it had not yet received the beautiful, distinct form we now see. It existed in a form of confusion before the form of disposition; all bodies were first created materially at once, then ordered over six days.
claims: Matter had a form of confusion before a form of disposition.

pll2d12c5-d1e3527.summary: Notes that the first question is resolved.

pll2d12c5-d1e3531.summary: Turns to the second question: where the matter existed and how high it reached.

pll2d12c5-d1e3546.summary: Answers, asserting nothing rashly, that the first mass came to be where it now subsists formed: earth settled in the middle, the other three elements mixed around it like a cloud so that it could not be seen, reaching as high as corporeal nature now extends.
claims: Unformed matter existed where the world now is.

pll2d12c5-d1e3567.summary: Reports some who think the mass extended beyond the firmament, denser below and finer above, and that from the finer part came the waters above the firmament.
claims: Some think the waters above the firmament came from the finer part of matter.

pll2d12c5-d1e3570.summary: States that such was the world's face in the beginning, before receiving form or disposition (Bede).

pll2d12c5-d1e3583.summary: Proposes to follow the order of that disposition.

pll2d12c5-d1e3586.summary: States that in six days God distinguished and formed all he had made materially at once, completed his work on the sixth, and rested on the seventh, ceasing to make new creatures; six kinds of things in six days, nothing made afterward outside them; yet he still works (John 5:17).
claims: God formed six kinds of things in six days.
God's rest means no new kinds of creature.

pl-l2d12c5.summary: Asks why the first matter is called unformed and where it existed. It was not wholly without form, since nothing bodily can lack all form, but it was in a form of confusion before the form of disposition: all bodies were first created materially at once in confusion, then ordered over six days. The mass of matter seems to have come to be where it now is, earth sinking in the middle, the other three elements mixed around it like a cloud, extending as high as corporeal nature now reaches, perhaps beyond the firmament, denser below and finer above; from the finer part some think came the waters above the firmament. In six days God distinguished six kinds of things and rested on the seventh, ceasing to make new creatures, though he still works (John 5:17).
claims: Unformed matter was not wholly without form, but in a form of confusion.
All bodies were created materially at once, then ordered over six days.
Unformed matter existed where the world now is, earth in the middle.
God distinguished six kinds of things in six days.
God's rest means he ceased to make new kinds of creatures, though he still works.
